doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The jingle business and its money
summary: Terry describes years of lucrative jingle sessions.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: Let’s talk about – when you got into – let’s talk about the jingle business. Are there products out there at some point that had Clark Terry’s trumpet behind them? Tell me some of those products and some of the jingles that you did.
I’ve done so many. We did them day after day, one session after the other, and I – sometimes I don’t even know what they are. You just go and say [Terry sings a melody]. “Next.”
What period were you doing this, if you can put dates on it? Was this in the early ’60s or . . .

It was in – it was after I came off the road, so it had to be, I guess, in the ’70s. ’60s and ’70s and, yeah, some ’80s. I did it for a whole lot of years. The cats who were doing that – it was so lucrative. All the cats bought their homes, their summer homes. Sent their kids to school in cars and all that. It was an extremely lucrative period.
How lucrative? Give me a sense of what the economics were.
I’m trying to figure. I know – I don’t remember the figures. It was a scale thing, but whatever the scale was at that time, you could do that all day long for day after day after day.
